title: A 2D camera with culling
description:
Write the core of a 2D renderer's camera.

- `toScreen(camera, worldX, worldY)` converts a world position to screen pixels: subtract the camera's position (the world point at the centre of the screen), multiply by the zoom, then add half the screen's width and height. Screen y grows downwards and so does world y here, so no flip is needed.
- `visible(camera, box)` says whether an axis-aligned world rectangle (`x`, `y` of its top-left corner, `w`, `h`) overlaps the area the camera shows. A box exactly touching the edge, with no overlap, is not visible.
- `cull(camera, boxes)` returns the indices of the visible boxes, in order.

```
camera at (100, 50), zoom 2, screen 800 x 600
toScreen(100, 50) = (400, 300)       the camera's centre is the screen's centre
toScreen(110, 50) = (420, 300)
the camera shows world x 100 ± 200 and y 50 ± 150
```
hints: `toScreen` is three steps: subtract the camera position, multiply by the zoom, add half the screen size.

The camera shows `screenW / 2 / zoom` world units either side of its x position, and `screenH / 2 / zoom` either side of its y. Two rectangles overlap when each starts before the other ends, on both axes; use strict `<` so touching edges do not count.
lessonTitle: A Tour of the Rendering Pipeline
